problem_type: New edges could enter the canvas through doors that never passed the connection admission gate
symptom: MCP / headless connect_canvas_edges wrote video -> text and audio -> text; paste, drag-duplicate, group duplicate, duplicate-as-variant and workflow-template instantiation copied illegal edges verbatim (Codex review 2 of #1137).
direct_cause: validateReferenceEdge lived in the renderer only; the headless canvasGraph.connectNodes checked endpoints / self-loop / duplicates, and four store actions appended cloned edges with state.edges = [...state.edges, ...cloned.edges].
class_root: There was no rule about which doors may put a new edge into the canvas and no admission function the main process could call, so each door either remembered to validate or did not.
affected_population: Every user / agent / MCP client that creates edges by any path other than manual connect and the Agent tool
Old projects holding edges the gate would refuse today (kept, ignored at execution)
entry_points: MCP connect_canvas_edges / create nodes with edges -> capabilityCore/core.connectProjectNodes -> canvasGraph.connectNodes
External whole-graph write-back (renderer applyExternalGraph and the on-disk gateway) -> mergeExternalCanvasWrite
Paste / Cmd+D / drag-duplicate -> store.pasteNodes; group duplicate -> duplicateGroupForDrag; duplicate-as-variant; workflow template instantiate -> appendAdmittedEdges
Manual connect / ring menu / @ / auto-reference / Agent connect_nodes / group links -> store.connectNodes / writeCanvasEdge (unchanged, already gated)
Undo / redo / restoreGraph / load / migration -> restore doors, deliberately not gated (they bring back edges that already existed)
internal_only_reason: Which node kind accepts which asset is a Nomi-domain rule (node-kind definitions), not decided by any third-party documentation.
invariants: A new edge reaches the canvas only through writeCanvasEdge, appendAdmittedEdges, headless canvasGraph.connectNodes, or mergeExternalCanvasWrite; each calls the one rule in electron/shared/canvas/edgeAdmission.
Edges already on the canvas (old projects) are never deleted by the gate; execution ignores kind-illegal ones except provenance (derived-output) edges.
check:canvas-edge-writers fails when a file outside the registered list writes .edges, when a listed file stops calling the gate, or when a bulk-append shape appears outside the allowed files.

Edges already on the canvas keep their id only while source/target/mode are unchanged; an external write that rewires an existing id is judged as a new edge (the original stays when refused). Undo/put-back goes through an explicit restoredEdgeIds restore write, not the external-new path.

door_reduction.why_not: The doors are different user actions (MCP, paste, group duplicate, variant, template, manual connect) that must keep existing; what was merged is the rule (one function in shared) and the whole-edge append (one function, four former copies). Former gap doors now call the same gate.

generality_proof: Every door that adds a new edge ends in validateReferenceEdge via admitNewEdges / writeCanvasEdge / headless connectNodes, and check:canvas-edge-writers makes a new unregistered writer, an ungated listed writer, or a bulk-append shape a red gate. Another vendor, platform or old project cannot bring a new path in without the list changing.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The one rule for whether a new edge may exist (target kind takes the input, source is referenceable, model archetype has a slot).
Batch admission: new ids pass the rule, known ids are kept untouched.
The only store function that appends whole edges to the canvas.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Calls validateReferenceEdge before pushing; skipped carries the reason code. Tests: canvasGraph.test.ts video/audio -> text, clip -> image.
Externally added edges go through admitNewEdges; used by both the renderer store and the on-disk gateway.
Appends via appendAdmittedEdges; covers drag-duplicate and Cmd+D which borrow the clipboard.
Restore doors bring back edges that already existed; gating them would delete user data. Tests keep a legacy illegal edge across delete + undo + redo + restoreGraph.
Restore write passes restoredEdgeIds through gateway.apply (disk and renderer) so legacy illegal edges come back; test in mcpSemanticOperationMatrix.test.ts.

recurrence.reason: Any new action, MCP tool or import that appends edges can skip the gate; earlier rounds (T8, B2) each patched one door.
same_class_scan: grep for .edges assignment and .edges.push in src and electron (non-test): every hit is registered in check:canvas-edge-writers or was routed through appendAdmittedEdges
node scripts/door-map.mjs connectNodes addEdge validateReferenceEdge: write doors enumerated and tabled in docs/plan/2026-10-10-edge-validation-all-entries.md
Probes from the review (video/audio -> text via the pure function, clipboard with illegal edge) turned into tests and mutation-checked red

prevention.invariant: No new edge exists unless validateReferenceEdge accepts it for the two endpoint nodes.
prevention.failure_mode: Rejected edges are skipped with a reason code (headless / agent) or a one-line notice (paste / copy / external write); nodes are still created.
prevention.strategy: One rule in the neutral layer, one append function in the store, the headless and merge paths call the same function, and a gate pins the list of files that may write .edges.

legacy_paths.rationale: The renderer copy of validateReferenceEdge and its helpers and the 17 inline connects literals were deleted; both now reference electron/shared/canvas/edgeAdmission.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party runtime controls this invariant.

migration: No data migration: old edges stay on the canvas and in project files; execution ignores kind-illegal ones. No file-format change.
residual_risks: No UI marks old illegal edges yet (product decision pending).
Restore doors (undo / load) are intentionally ungated; a future restore that fabricates edges would not be caught by this gate.

Provenance (derived-output) edges carry no marker, so resolveGenerationReferences keeps them by kind pair (derivedOutput rules): an old hand-drawn clip -> video edge is treated as provenance and may become a video reference. A marker field would need a product/data decision and was not invented here.

structural_evidence.behavior_preservation: validateReferenceEdge keeps its order of checks (input false, text prompt edge, referenceable source, asset list, archetype slots); it is now split into validateEdgeKinds plus the archetype-slot half called inside the same function. Renderer callers import the same names from referenceEdgeCapability (re-exported). The only intended change: unknown node kinds are refused instead of depending on the registry lookup.
structural_evidence.verification_limits: Unit tests, typecheck, i18n, boundaries and the wide vitest run over generationCanvas / capability / project / creation / electron ran on Windows; no real-Electron walk and no macOS run on this line.
